name: Verath & Lund Lambswool Crewneck
description:
Verath & Lund has been making knitwear in the Scandinavian-minimalist tradition since the 2140s, and the Lambswool Crewneck is as close to a house signature as the brand gets — a simple, clean silhouette in a mid-weight lambswool blend that they source from a single cooperative farm in what used to be Norway. The neck is a true crew, not too high and not too wide, and the body is slightly relaxed without being oversized. It comes in a restrained palette: oatmeal, slate, charcoal, and one seasonal color each year (2199 was a dusty rose that sold out in ten days).

The fabric has a slight texture to it — not scratchy, but present. You know you're wearing wool. It pills slightly after heavy use, which Verath & Lund addresses with a complimentary depilling service at their boutiques. The sweater is the kind of thing that gets worn for fifteen years and still looks considered. Tier 3 and Tier 4 buyers make up most of the market. It requires hand washing or a gentle cycle with cold water and the appropriate bag, and the care instructions are printed on a small woven label inside the left hem in both Norwegian and Standard.
materials: woven label with bilingual care instructions
what_it_says: You buy fewer things and better things. You've been wearing this since it was new and you'll wear it when it's old.
worn_by: people who think carefully about their wardrobe
story_hooks: The Norwegian cooperative farm that supplies Verath & Lund's lambswool is the subject of a quiet land dispute with a corponation expanding its agricultural holdings north.
A particular oatmeal crewneck has been handed down through three generations of a family in Tier 3 — and the current owner has just been offered a job in the Spire.
Someone is selling convincing Verath & Lund fakes on the gray market — convincing enough that even the boutique staff can't always tell without the interior label check.
